done_when: When an item's CI checks were cancelled and none failed, close starts them again or waits for the newer run instead of sending the item to a worker round

known.title: Do not treat a different event's completed run as a passing check
Not done: Cancelled checks are still reported as failed
Honor the single retry when close is restarted

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - one workflow runs different jobs for pull requests and manual dispatches on the same commit. If its pull-request `tests` job is cancelled and a newer dispatch run completes without running that job, the workflow ID and run number match this condition, so the cancelled `tests` check becomes PASS. Event-dependent job names are already used in `.github/workflows/forge.yml:97`; a skipped dispatch job with a different name does not satisfy or fail `tests`. `_pending` at `src/forge/checks.py:365` then counts the old cancelled check as the required passing check, allowing close to report green without successful PR tests. [GitHub supports event-specific jobs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow).
findings.title: Do not treat a different event's completed run as a passing check

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a cancelled Actions workflow contains multiple jobs, as the matrix in `.github/workflows/forge.yml:41` does. After starting the first job's workflow again, the next cancelled job has the same run ID and reaches line 352 with the original completed snapshot, so it stays RED and close recommends `forge work` immediately. GitHub puts a workflow's jobs in one check suite ([GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/use-workflow-run-logs)). The same classification also occurs for a cancelled third-party check with no matching Actions run at lines 344-346. When an existing rerun is already running, lines 347-353 can try to start it again instead of waiting: GitHub retains the run number across attempts. The unmet item is: "When an item's CI checks were cancelled and none failed, close starts them again or waits for the newer run instead of sending the item to a worker round".
findings.title: Not done: Cancelled checks are still reported as failed

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a cancelled workflow is rerun, is cancelled again, and the user runs close again on the same head. The `rerun` set is recreated for every wait, so the new invocation starts the same workflow yet again instead of honoring the recorded one-retry limit. Repeated cancellations and restarts can keep consuming CI time without reaching the intended stop. GitHub exposes an attempt number that persists across reruns ([GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables)).
Adds work: recognize an already retried workflow when close restarts; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Honor the single retry when close is restarted

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a rerun remains pending or is cancelled a second time. The first two named proofs assert only a successful close and the rerun-call count; they would still pass if close returned before reading the pending and green answers. The third proof supplies only the original cancelled check and completed workflow, which the queue repeats (`tests/test_land.py:73`); it never supplies a new attempt that was cancelled. It therefore passes when the original cancellation is immediately mistaken for a second cancellation, and it does not verify the claimed worker dispatch.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_close_reruns_cancelled_ci.py

why: Issue 1661: close treats cancelled CI checks as failed and gives forge work as the next step, so a worker round runs, finds nothing and hands back (6 times in one client day).
